positioning: The cat of Norse legend. A mountain-climbing giant in a weatherproof coat.
story: The Norwegian Forest Cat, called the Wegie for short, is the stuff of Viking legend. These big longhairs have lived in Norway for centuries, and they appear in Norse myth as the cats that pulled the goddess Freya's chariot. King Olav V named the breed the official cat of Norway.

It is built for a cold, wet climate. A long double coat with a dense woolly underlayer sheds rain and snow, topped by a full ruff, tufted lynx-tipped ears, and a long bushy tail. Big and muscular, the Wegie is a powerful climber that descends trees head-first.

For all its wild looks, the temperament is gentle and friendly. The Norwegian Forest Cat is calm, patient, and sociable, fond of its family without being demanding, and happy to watch the household from a high perch.

It is often confused with the Maine Coon, and the two share a similar size and rugged build, but they developed an ocean apart and differ in head shape and coat. The Wegie is slow to mature, reaching full size at around five years.

The Wegie is a calm, friendly giant that likes to survey its home from up high. It is sociable without being clingy, patient with children and other pets, and content to spend part of the day on its own, though it enjoys company when it is offered.

The water-shedding double coat needs regular brushing, with a heavy molt in spring that calls for daily attention. The breed is sturdy but can carry the heart condition HCM, a kidney condition, and a rare metabolic disorder called GSD IV, so reputable breeders test for them.
fblocks: Named for the forests of Norway, where it lived for centuries, and tied to Norse myth as Freya's cat.
An ancient Scandinavian forest cat shaped by climate, later named the national cat of Norway.
Sociable and easygoing, it loves to climb and perch. The thick coat needs regular brushing, especially in spring.
A long, water-shedding double coat with a ruff, tufted ears, and bushy tail, in many colors and patterns.
Reaches full size at around five years. Similar to the Maine Coon but a distinct, separately developed breed.
Offer tall perches, regular brushing, and easygoing company. The Wegie is independent but affectionate on its own terms.
Can carry the heart condition HCM and a rare metabolic disorder, so choose breeders who screen their lines.
days: The Norwegian Forest Cat wears a waterproof coat over a wool undercoat.
Norse myth gave the goddess Freya a chariot pulled by two giant cats.
It takes up to five years to reach full size and full glory.
Nothing says winter like a Wegie asleep in the hay, tail over its nose.
The best seat in the barn is the doorway, with a view and no wind.
King Olav V is said to have made it Norway's official cat. Ask your friends.
After the snow and the chores, a Wegie tucks in one paw and sleeps.
last_walk:
The path is white and the cabin light is on.
A Norwegian Forest Cat has crossed this snow a thousand times. It walks without hurry, tail high, as if the forest were its own front yard. When it reaches the door, it does not ask to come in. It waits, because it knows the warm room is already waiting for it.
